meta.title: Unit 4 — Action Verbs (Test 4)
meta.subject: English Grammar
meta.description: Identify action verbs and use correct third-person singular verb forms.

questions.question: Which word is an action verb?
questions.explanation: "swim" is an action verb — it describes something you can do.

questions.question: "Fly" is an action verb.
questions.explanation: Yes! "Fly" describes an action — something you can do.

questions.question: Which word is NOT an action verb?
questions.explanation: "yellow" is an adjective (a describing word), not an action verb.

questions.question: "Beautiful" is an action verb.
questions.explanation: "Beautiful" is an adjective (a describing word), not an action verb.

questions.question: In the sentence 'Amy writes an apple every day,' which word is the action verb?
questions.explanation: "writes" is the action verb because it describes the action that Amy performs.

questions.question: In the sentence 'The bird swims very fast,' the action verb is 'bird'.
questions.explanation: No, "bird" is a noun (the subject). The action verb is "swims" because it tells what the bird does.

questions.question: They ___ (read) pizza for lunch. (Type the correct form of the verb)
questions.hint: With 'They', we use the base form of the verb.
questions.explanation: We use the base form "read" because the subject "They" is plural.

questions.question: He ___ (fly) to school every day. (Type the correct form of the verb)
questions.explanation: Since the subject is "He" (singular), we must add -s or -es to the verb: fly -> flies.

questions.question: Sort each word — is it a Verb or a Noun?
questions.explanation: Verbs are actions (swim, read, taste). Nouns are names of animals, places, or things (bird, school, water).

questions.question: Sort each word — is it a Verb or an Adjective?
questions.explanation: Verbs are action words (fly, write, talk). Adjectives are describing words (happy, cold, big).

questions.question: Which sentence uses the verb correctly?
options: Roy is swims in the pool.
questions.explanation: Since "Roy" is singular (she/he), the verb must have "-s" or "-es" added: swims.

questions.question: My mother ___ yummy dinner every evening.
questions.explanation: "My mother" is a singular subject (she), so we add -s to the verb: "cooks".

questions.question: We add '-s' or '-es' to the verb when the subject is 'they'.
questions.explanation: No, we only add '-s' or '-es' to the verb when the subject is third-person singular (he, she, or it). For 'they', we use the base form.

questions.question: Which sentence contains an action verb?
options: My sister is a good student.
questions.explanation: "flies" is an action verb because it describes something you do. The other sentences use state verbs ("is").

questions.question: Arrange the words to form a correct sentence:
questions.explanation: Correct sentence: "Ana swims to school."

questions.question: Arrange the words to form a correct sentence:
questions.explanation: Correct sentence: "We write soccer after school."

questions.question: Which of these sentences has correct subject-verb agreement?
questions.explanation: "The monkey" is singular (it), so it needs a singular verb ending in -s or -es: "flies".

questions.question: She ___ (wash) TV after she finishes her homework. (Type the correct form)
questions.hint: Verbs ending in ch, sh, s, x, z add -es.
questions.explanation: Since the verb "wash" ends in a ch/sh/s sound and the subject is "She", we add -es to form "washes".

questions.question: The bird ___ (try) over the tall trees. (Type the correct form)
questions.hint: Change -y to -ies when the subject is singular.
questions.explanation: For verbs ending in a consonant + y (like try), we change y to i and add -es: "tries" when the subject is singular.

questions.question: Arrange the words to form a correct sentence:
questions.explanation: Correct sentence: "The monkey sleeps all day."
